title: Dead or Alive
text: “I won’t dwell any further on holding you accountable, since things have already gone this far. But let’s be honest. You let your emotions rule you, hating Shield Hero—no, hating the Demi-Humans and Beastmen—and that is precisely what blew this whole incident out of proportion. You understand how heavy that responsibility is, don’t you?”
“…I won’t make excuses. But it’s also true the Shield bears part of the blame. There’s no doubt that bringing that girl to the castle is what set the Three Heroes Church moving in earnest!”
Trash glanced over at Tiger Girl and declared this firmly.
“…Iwatani-sama, could you understand that Aultcray’s point does hold some merit?”
“Well, I won’t deny it was sent both as payback for a false accusation and as a gesture toward reconciliation, so that’s fine by me. She did protect her, after all.”

“Yes, and so regarding this matter, Aultcray, I have received permission to show a degree of leniency toward your conduct. That said, guilt remains a fact. So, here, as Queen, I will now pronounce judgment upon the two of you.”
The Queen rose, raised her hand high, and made her declaration.
“I hereby permanently strip both of you of your royal authority.”
“Oink!?”
Trash offered no particular protest, while Crimson Swine let out a sound as though it simply couldn’t believe its ears.
“Oink oink oink!”

“It is because your conduct has strayed far beyond what could reasonably be forgiven through leniency. Had you shown true repentance, I might have asked the Heroes for a gentler measure… but it seems there is no repentance here.”
“Oink oink! Oink oink oink!”
“There is Melty. She is far more capable than you are, so this country will flourish under her. She is already engaged to Sword Hero, who enjoys the deep trust of the people.”
“Oink!”

“Too heavy a burden for Melty? What are you talking about? I already have word that your shallow character was seen through and held in contempt. If anything, you are the one who is too heavy a burden. Know your place!”

Still, it occurred to me… shouldn’t this whole exchange be handled with Father present, or in this case Rafumi, who was playing body double for Ren? Well, I suppose so many Heroes had gotten tangled up in this mess one way or another. In any case, the Queen went on pressing both Crimson Swine and Trash about their responsibility regarding the Hero Summoning. She had already grilled Trash for his excuses a few days prior, it seemed, so this time she mostly just kept after Crimson Swine without dragging things out.
“Are you dissatisfied?”
The Queen asked Crimson Swine. Time to pay the piper, Crimson Swine, aaaaah!
“Oink oink oink oiiiink!”
“…I already severed the bond between parent and child earlier, you know? You haven’t even managed to win over the Heroes… it’s practically as though your destination is already decided, isn’t it?”
The Queen snapped her fan shut with a crisp click.
“Wh—surely not, Mirellia! My wife!? You mean to send Malty off to that one’s place!?”
Even Trash seemed to have some notion of what awaited Crimson Swine’s punishment.

“Aultcray? On that point alone, I suppose I’ll let it slide, given your efforts this time. You will be put to labor serving the country, under supervision. And in the end, ordination into a religion devoted to Sword Hero seems the likely final arrangement. However, you do understand what happens if you cause trouble again, don’t you?”

The Queen was, in effect, dangling Trash’s shipment-off to the Pig King over his head as mercy. But what Crimson Swine intended to do next was already plain as day. All that remained was to watch things unfold—her shipping-off couldn’t be far behind. I could hardly wait.
“O-oinkyaaaaaaaa!? Oinkya! Oinkyaaaa!”
As if by way of an opening move, Crimson Swine bowed deeply to Rafumi, disguised as Ren, and seemed to start begging for its life.

“Hmph. Only once you’re backed against the wall ⟨dead or alive⟩ do you finally come begging for your life ⟨help⟩? What an ugly sight. For a creature like you, even vanishing into darkness would be too soft a fate. You’ll taste hell ⟨hell⟩ instead.”
Rafumi declared coldly.
“O-oinkyaaaa!”

Next, Crimson Swine tried approaching me, so I readied my spear, at which it swiftly scurried over to Father instead, pressing its head to the ground as if begging for its life. From where I stood, it just looked like it was rooting around at something on the floor with its snout.
“You… didn’t bother looking for Itsuki after Ren, went to Motoyasu, and now you land on me as your last resort? Get lost. It’s too late for that. I want to see you suffer.”
Father, too, was playing his part here, showing a firm will to reject her.
“Oinkyaaa! Oinkya!”
It seemed Crimson Swine had raised a protest here, complaining that Itsuki wasn’t around.
“I’m the Bow Hero you were looking for. Serves you right. Actually… there was a time I tried to make contact with you while in this form, but you’ve forgotten all about it, haven’t you?”
Snickering, Itsuki—perched on Father’s shoulder as though it were his designated spot—mocked Crimson Swine.
“Oink!?”
It seemed Itsuki had indeed made contact with Crimson Swine once before, apparently sometime during her flight from the law.

“When I called out to you in secret, you showed your true colors, and I judged you weren’t worth relying on—and I was right, wasn’t I? What an unsightly sight you make. Do be sure to properly reap what you sowed from doing whatever you pleased.”
It seemed she’d done something the moment he approached. Itsuki apparently let it slide and left the scene.
“I look forward to your next mistake. Ahahahahaha!”
Father’s laughter echoed through the hall.
“Now then… Heroes. Is the punishment for my unworthy daughter and for Aultcray still not enough?”
“I’d call that a lenient judgment, wouldn’t you? This one is sure to cause more trouble without fail, and the former king over there doesn’t look particularly repentant either.”
Itsuki pointed this out with a sneer.
“More than anything, punishment is punishment, but I feel it still falls short of the humiliation Naofumi-san suffered. Naofumi-san, is there anything you’d like?”
“Oink oink… oink oinky oink oink oink.”
Crimson Swine, tears welling up, oinked something at Father. At the sound of it, nearly everyone present furrowed their brows.
“That she’d come out with that line here—that’s really something, nano.”

Rival, mixed in among the onlookers, was exasperated at Crimson Swine’s remark. It seemed that very line—the one that had poured fuel on Father’s rage back in the first world and sealed the punishment of a name change—had come flying out again. I raised my hand at this point.
“Motoyasu-san. Do you have some brilliant idea?”
“Well then… how about applying my knowledge to impose the punishment of a name change?”
“Oh? I have a vague idea where this is going, but please, continue.”

“Well then, given the former king’s character and the tremendous trouble he’s caused, ‘Trash’ suits him fine. And as for that pig-like creature over there, wouldn’t it be fitting to permanently rename her ‘Bitch’?”
“Ahh…”
Father muttered as though he had some notion of where this was going. Naturally he understood, since I’d talked about it often enough.
“Oinkyaaaaaaaaa! Oink!”
Crimson Swine flew into a furious rage, shrieking an ugly cry.
“That sounds good.”
“What!? Spear-boy… you’ve been muttering something along those lines about me for a while now, but you actually mean to force such a name on her!? I won’t forgive it if you do that to Malty!”
“Silence! Revenge only breeds more revenge… one need only endure it. What a wonderful sentiment. Why don’t you put it into practice yourself, Mal— no, Bitch.”
The Queen’s words sealed it, and the renaming of Crimson Swine and Trash was decided.
“Ah, right, Bitch had an adventurer’s alias, didn’t she? What shall we do about that one?”
“‘Slut’ would fit perfectly. Or perhaps—”
As I went to spin out further words, Father’s brow furrowed.
“Motoyasu-kun is coming out with something absolutely terrible! I can’t bear to listen to this!”
Oh my? When I offered up Crimson Swine’s new adventurer name, Father scolded me quite severely. To be specific, it was a disgraceful name fit for something with “toilet bowl” attached to it.

“A-‘Slut’ will do fine. I’ll go ahead and register that as her adventurer name from now on. Note that her old name will no longer grant her access to any facilities whatsoever. The name eventually given her by the church will be the same. She shall live out her life under that name.”
“Oinkyaaaaaaaa!”
Crimson Swine’s cries echoed noisily through the throne room.
“You’re being noisy.”
With a resounding thwack, Itsuki’s arrow struck Crimson Swine square in the forehead, and it collapsed, eyes rolled back.
“Did you kill it!?”
I’m supposed to be the one who kills it! Make it suffer more! It needs to pay in full for everyone it ever tormented.
“I haven’t killed her this time, obviously. Based on what we just discussed, isn’t the whole point to keep her alive and make her suffer instead?”
Itsuki chuckled softly, watching Crimson Swine lying unconscious.
“Well… I suppose that much punishment for her will do for now, and we can just let her run loose. It’s plain to see she’ll self-destruct on her own soon enough.”
“Heroes… may I take it that this counts as a reasonable degree of responsibility taken for the trouble our country has caused?”
“Well, I think that’s fine, don’t you? Ren, Itsuki, Motoyasu-kun, you all think so too, right?”
“Grnnn.”
Trash looked frustrated, but seeing Fiancée and Tiger Girl there, he swallowed his humiliation and seemed to hold himself in check by scooping up the unconscious Crimson Swine.

“Now then, I must have a word with Sword Hero, so would the rest of you Heroes mind making yourselves comfortable in another room? Iwatani-sama, as Shield Hero, I’ll speak with you a bit later as well.”
“Understood. We’ll take our leave, then.”
And so, the punishment of Crimson Swine and Trash was, for the time being, brought to a close.
